page.layout: One heading at the top, centred: PRÆFATIO. Below it one column of running text, set in italic. A catchword sits at the lower right, below the last line.

p.i: imo etiam Monarchiam tem-poralem supra omnes Reges ac Principes sibi vindicârunt, & quidem (quod probè notandum) ex eo ipso fundamento, quod potestatem Ecclesiasticam omnem ad se transtulissent. Unde inferebant, multò magis temporalem potestatem ad se pertinere, quemadmodum apud Bellarmi-num lib. s.[?] de Pontif. Rom. capp. s.[?] 6. &c. videre est: qui cum suis Theologis longè astutius Papæ potestatem temporalem astruit, dum eam ex Spirituali seu Ecclesiasticâ derivat, quàm Canonistæ, qui illam di-

page.notes: The scan is a clear page with no margin notes. Below the last line, next to "di-", there is a printed "(?)" followed by "s", which I have read as a catchword; the "(?)" is printed and I have not included it. The numerals in "lib. s." and "capp. s." look like old-style 5 and are marked [?]; the context (Bellarmine, De Pontifice Romano, lib. 5, cap. 6) suggests 5 is intended. The printed "s" forms are transcribed as plain s. The page is marked with a Google digitiser watermark at the lower right, which is not transcribed.
